# `generator-shortcuts`

The strongest plausible source-bound shortcut is **`unseen_directions_continue_straight`**: use the correct canonical transition table except that a color-4 slash approached from the west and a color-5 backslash approached from the north do not turn; the ray continues straight. This single rival subsumes the two individual partial-table shortcuts.

It fits all four labeled canonical pairs. None of those rays contains either missing incoming-direction case, so the rival is observationally identical on the entire canonical demonstration set.

## Exact disagreement input

## How the output was checked

The exact input was generated from the final source, passed `self_check()`, and was evaluated through the public `Catalog.apply(..., reference="canonical")` Racket authority. The receipt reports `rule_hash_matches_catalog: true`, `valid_output: true`, and no error. A separately implemented oracle in `workspace/reference_probe.py` agrees with the Racket grid. The focused regression regenerates the input, verifies the saved authority output, verifies that the shortcut fits every usable canonical pair, and checks the exact 21-cell difference list.

## Does the proposed generator emit such cases?

Yes. Both `full_direction_probe_compact` and `full_direction_probe_wide` exercise slash-from-west and backslash-from-north. They occupy alternating probe slots 1, 3, 5, and 7 of the eight-slot default schedule. Every contiguous four-pair lesson therefore contains two such probes; with three demonstrations and any one query held out, at least one probe remains visible. This was checked exhaustively over all eight schedule starts in the task tests and sampled more broadly in the semantic gate and 300-lesson rotation census.
